description: Success (S-) and failure (F-) scenarios that define what a correct gitopsctl looks like. Each scenario names the automated check that decides it. Weights: critical=5, high=3, medium=2, low=1.

verdict_rules.PASS: no failed critical or high scenario and score >= 95
verdict_rules.CONDITIONAL: no failed critical scenario and score >= 80

gates.title: Unit tests pass with the race detector
Total statement coverage is at least 80%
No known vulnerabilities in called code

scenarios.title: Binary builds and exposes the documented commands
scenarios.when: The binary is built and run with --help
scenarios.then: Exit 0; start, register-apps, register-cluster, sync-app, approve-app, diff-app, check-cluster, dashboard, list-apps and unregister are listed; start lists --api-token, --api-token-file, --api-cors-origin
scenarios.if_failing: A command or flag was removed or renamed. Restore it or update docs and this scenario deliberately.

scenarios.title: Manifests from Git are applied with ownership labels
scenarios.given: A registered cluster and an auto-sync app pointing at a repo with one ConfigMap
scenarios.when: The controller starts
scenarios.then: The app reaches Synced/Healthy; the ConfigMap exists with the manifest data and labels app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=gitopsctl, gitopsctl.io/app, gitopsctl.io/cluster; last_synced_git_hash equals repo HEAD; consecutive_failures is 0
scenarios.if_failing: Check internal/core/k8s ApplyManifests/processYAMLData and internal/controller performSync.

scenarios.title: An unchanged commit causes no further cluster writes
scenarios.when: Several poll intervals pass with no new commit
scenarios.then: The cluster receives zero additional create/update/delete requests
scenarios.if_failing: performSync must return early when trigger is poll and the commit hash equals LastSyncedGitHash.

scenarios.title: A new commit propagates to the cluster
scenarios.when: A commit changes a manifest
scenarios.then: The live object is updated and last_synced_git_hash equals the new HEAD
scenarios.if_failing: Polling, git pull, or the update path regressed.

scenarios.title: Manual sync policy holds changes until approved, then applies them
scenarios.when: A commit exists, then approve-app is run for that commit
scenarios.then: Status is OutOfSync and nothing is applied before approval; after approval the app reaches Synced and the resource exists
scenarios.if_failing: Approvals are stored on the shared application; the reconciler works on a copy and must refresh ApprovedGitHash in performSync.

scenarios.title: diff-app reports create, update and unchanged without writing to the cluster
scenarios.given: A manual-policy app with pending changes
scenarios.when: diff-app runs before and after approval and after a new commit
scenarios.then: Output lists + create, ~ update, = unchanged with correct totals; the cluster receives zero mutating requests during diff-app
scenarios.if_failing: Plan must stay read-only (Get only) and compare desired as a subset of live.

scenarios.title: Removed manifests are deleted when prune is enabled
scenarios.given: A prune-enabled app with resources keep and drop plus an unrelated object owned by another app
scenarios.when: drop.yaml is removed from Git
scenarios.then: drop is deleted; keep and the other app's object remain
scenarios.if_failing: Check internal/core/k8s Prune and that saveAppStatus persists AppliedResources.

scenarios.title: Removed manifests stay when prune is disabled (default)
scenarios.when: A manifest is removed from Git
scenarios.then: The live resource is untouched
scenarios.if_failing: Pruning must be strictly opt-in. Treat any default-on deletion as a release blocker.

scenarios.title: Health and metrics are reachable without a token
scenarios.when: GET /health and /metrics without credentials
scenarios.then: Both return 200
scenarios.if_failing: Auth middleware must only wrap the /api/v1 group.

scenarios.title: A valid token can list applications and clusters
scenarios.when: GET /api/v1/applications and /clusters with an admin token
scenarios.then: 200 with JSON arrays containing the registered resources
scenarios.if_failing: Authentication rejects valid credentials or the list endpoints changed shape.

scenarios.title: Token scopes gate read, sync and admin operations
scenarios.when: Each token calls GET, POST /sync and DELETE endpoints
scenarios.then: read: GET only; sync: GET and POST /sync|/approve|/check|/plan; admin: everything; others get 403
scenarios.if_failing: See internal/api/auth.go requiredScope; every new mutating route must be mapped deliberately.

scenarios.title: Mutating calls are audited without leaking the token
scenarios.when: It triggers a sync
scenarios.then: An io.gitopsctl.api.audit event with method, path, status and a non-secret token_id appears in event history; the token never appears
scenarios.if_failing: Audit emission or token_id derivation regressed.

scenarios.title: Without a token the API binds to loopback only
scenarios.when: start --api-address :PORT
scenarios.then: A warning is logged and the API is not reachable on non-loopback interfaces
scenarios.if_failing: An unauthenticated API on all interfaces can modify remote clusters. Block release.

scenarios.title: Registration persists state and leaves no temp files
scenarios.when: register-cluster then register-apps --prune run
scenarios.then: clusters.json and applications.json contain the entries (prune true); list-apps shows the app; no .tmp- files remain in configs/
scenarios.if_failing: State writes must go through common.WriteFileAtomic.

scenarios.title: Example configs load and every start flag is documented
scenarios.when: list-apps and list-clusters run; start --help is compared with docs
scenarios.then: The example app and cluster are listed with their repo and cluster names; each start flag appears in docs/cli-reference.md or docs/configuration.md
scenarios.if_failing: Config JSON keys are snake_case (repo_url, cluster_name, kubeconfig_path...). Fix docs/examples, not the loader.

scenarios.title: Release supply chain is hardened
scenarios.when: Static checks run
scenarios.then: LICENSE is Apache-2.0; GoReleaser configures checksum, sboms, signs and docker_signs; Dockerfile base is digest-pinned; every workflow action is SHA-pinned; workflow go-version equals go.mod; no @latest tool installs
scenarios.if_failing: Resolve new action tags to commit SHAs (gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/TAG --jq .sha).

scenarios.title: Missing, wrong or non-bearer credentials are rejected
scenarios.when: Requests carry no token, a wrong token, or a Basic scheme
scenarios.then: 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and no data in the body
scenarios.if_failing: Authentication bypass. Block release.

scenarios.title: Insufficient scope is refused and state is untouched
scenarios.when: It calls DELETE /applications/web
scenarios.then: 403 and the application still exists
scenarios.if_failing: Privilege escalation. Block release.

scenarios.title: Unknown resources and malformed bodies fail cleanly
scenarios.when: sync, plan or approve target an unknown app; registration body is malformed JSON
scenarios.then: 404 for unknown apps (including approve), 400 for malformed JSON; the controller stays alive
scenarios.if_failing: Handlers must validate existence before queueing work.

scenarios.title: Secrets never appear in process output
scenarios.given: A controller running with tokens and a CLI using --api-token
scenarios.when: Good and bad requests are made
scenarios.then: No token value appears in controller logs or CLI output
scenarios.if_failing: Remove the token from log fields, error messages and request logging.

scenarios.title: Corrupt state stops startup without being overwritten
scenarios.when: start runs
scenarios.then: Non-zero exit with 'failed to load applications'; the file is byte-for-byte unchanged
scenarios.if_failing: Never write state before it has been loaded successfully.

scenarios.title: A malformed token file stops startup
scenarios.given: A token file with a line lacking a scope
scenarios.when: start --api-token-file runs
scenarios.then: Non-zero exit mentioning the token file; the API never starts unauthenticated
scenarios.if_failing: Fail closed on invalid auth configuration.

scenarios.title: Invalid application registrations are rejected without side effects
scenarios.when: register-apps gets a bad URL, interval below 10s, bad sync policy, unknown cluster or missing args
scenarios.then: Every call exits non-zero and applications.json gains no entries
scenarios.if_failing: Validation must run before any state is written.

scenarios.title: Invalid cluster registrations are rejected without side effects
scenarios.when: register-cluster gets a missing, invalid or directory kubeconfig or an invalid name
scenarios.then: Every call exits non-zero and clusters.json gains no entries
scenarios.if_failing: Validation must run before any state is written.

scenarios.title: A cluster API outage is reported and the app recovers on its own
scenarios.when: The controller starts, then the outage ends
scenarios.then: Status Error with 'Apply error' and failures >= 1 while the controller stays alive; afterwards the app converges to Synced without a restart
scenarios.if_failing: reconcileApp must keep polling after a failed sync whenever a cluster client exists.

scenarios.title: An unreachable Git repository is reported and the app recovers
scenarios.given: A repo path that does not exist yet
scenarios.when: The controller starts and the repo later appears
scenarios.then: Status Error with 'Git error' and failures >= 1; once reachable the app syncs without a restart
scenarios.if_failing: Git failures must be transient, not terminal.

scenarios.title: Namespace restrictions block forbidden resources
scenarios.given: A cluster limited to namespace demo
scenarios.when: A manifest targets namespace prod
scenarios.then: Nothing is created; status Error explains the namespace is not in the allowed list
scenarios.if_failing: isNamespaceAllowed must gate apply, prune and health checks.

scenarios.title: Sync failures are never masked by the health check
scenarios.given: An app with healthy previously-applied resources
scenarios.when: A sync fails or is held OutOfSync
scenarios.then: Status stays Error/OutOfSync and is not overwritten by Healthy
scenarios.if_failing: checkHealth must only run for Synced/Healthy/Progressing/Degraded.

scenarios.title: Resources not owned by the app survive pruning
scenarios.given: A prune-enabled app whose stale live object lost its ownership labels
scenarios.when: Its manifest is removed from Git
scenarios.then: The object is not deleted
scenarios.if_failing: Prune must verify managed-by and gitopsctl.io/app labels before deleting.

scenarios.title: Mass deletion is refused
scenarios.when: 12 manifests are removed at once
scenarios.then: Status Error 'Prune error'; all resources remain
scenarios.if_failing: The max-deletions guard (k8s.DefaultMaxPrune) was bypassed.

scenarios.title: Nothing is pruned while the same sync fails to apply
scenarios.when: A commit removes a manifest and adds one the cluster rejects
scenarios.then: The stale resource is kept while the apply fails and is pruned after recovery
scenarios.if_failing: Prune must run only after a fully successful apply.

scenarios.title: Shutdown is safe under concurrent commands
scenarios.when: Stop is called twice or while commands are being sent
scenarios.then: No panic, no deadlock, no blocked senders, race detector clean
scenarios.if_failing: Do not close command channels; senders must select on ctx.Done().

scenarios.title: State files are written atomically and corrupt state is rejected
scenarios.when: They are saved, or loaded when truncated or invalid
scenarios.then: Writes go via temp file and rename with no leftovers; corrupt files return errors, never partial data
scenarios.if_failing: A crash mid-write must never leave truncated JSON.

scenarios.title: An agent can create a session, deploy into it and tear it down
scenarios.given: A controller started with --agents-file and an agent token
scenarios.when: The agent creates a session, deploys a git path and deletes the session
scenarios.then: A labelled namespace with a quota exists; manifests are applied inside it and labelled as owned by the session; deletion removes the namespace and its contents
scenarios.if_failing: The core agent workflow is broken. Check internal/session and the /sessions handlers before anything else.

scenarios.title: Redeploying a session prunes resources removed from git
scenarios.given: A session with two deployed objects
scenarios.when: One object is removed from git and the session is redeployed
scenarios.then: The removed object is deleted, the other is updated
scenarios.if_failing: Session.Resources is not handed to Apply as Previous, or Prune ownership labels no longer match.

scenarios.title: Sessions survive a controller restart
scenarios.when: The controller is stopped and started again
scenarios.then: The session is still active with its resources and can be redeployed; its namespace is untouched
scenarios.if_failing: Session persistence or startup reconciliation is deleting or forgetting live sessions.

scenarios.title: Expired sessions are removed, live ones are kept
scenarios.given: One expired and one live session and a stopped controller
scenarios.when: The controller starts
scenarios.then: The expired session's namespace and record are removed; the live session is kept
scenarios.if_failing: The janitor does not reap on startup or compares expiry incorrectly.

scenarios.title: Compliant manifests pass the policy and land in the session namespace
scenarios.given: A policy and a compliant Deployment or ConfigMap
scenarios.when: The manifests are checked and applied
scenarios.then: No violations; unscoped objects default to the session namespace
scenarios.if_failing: The policy is rejecting safe manifests or changing behaviour for clients without a policy.

scenarios.title: The policy rejects every unsafe manifest class and fails closed
scenarios.given: Manifests with privileged containers, root users, host access, foreign images, RBAC, cluster-scoped objects, wrong namespaces, spoofed labels, unknown kinds or malformed YAML; and invalid policy files
scenarios.when: They are checked, applied or planned
scenarios.then: Each is rejected with a named rule; nothing is applied, not even compliant objects in the same set; invalid policy files fail to load
scenarios.if_failing: A rule was weakened or bypassed. Fix the policy engine; never loosen the scenario.

scenarios.title: Unsafe workloads are rejected end to end with 422 and never reach the cluster
scenarios.given: A session and a repository containing a privileged, root, foreign-registry, capability-adding or over-replicated Deployment next to a compliant object
scenarios.when: The agent deploys
scenarios.then: 422 with the violated rule; neither the Deployment nor the compliant object is created
scenarios.if_failing: Policy is not enforced on the session deploy path, or apply is no longer all-or-nothing.

scenarios.title: Cluster-scoped, RBAC, other-namespace and label-spoofing manifests are blocked
scenarios.given: A session and a repository with a ClusterRoleBinding, Namespace, kube-system object, reserved label or disallowed kind
scenarios.when: The agent deploys
scenarios.then: 422 and zero writes to the cluster
scenarios.if_failing: An escape from the session namespace exists. Treat as a security incident.

scenarios.title: Agent tokens are confined to their own sessions
scenarios.given: Two agents plus read, sync and admin tokens
scenarios.when: They call session and non-session endpoints, and one agent targets the other's session
scenarios.then: Cross-agent access is 404; agent tokens get 403 outside /sessions; read and sync tokens get 403 on /sessions; missing or wrong tokens get 401; impersonation is 403
scenarios.if_failing: Authorisation or ownership lookup is leaking across agents.

scenarios.title: Repository allowlist, path and ref validation hold
scenarios.given: A session and hostile deploy requests
scenarios.when: The repo is not allowlisted or is a local path, the path escapes the repo or is absolute, the ref looks like a git option or contains .., or a manifest is a symlink
scenarios.then: 403 or 400 with zero cluster writes
scenarios.if_failing: Input validation in session.Deploy regressed; this allows reading host files or arbitrary clones.

scenarios.title: Session limits and TTL bounds are enforced
scenarios.given: An agent at its session limit
scenarios.when: It creates another session, or asks for an excessive or malformed ttl, or an admin names an unknown agent
scenarios.then: 429, 400, 400 and 403 respectively, and no namespace is created
scenarios.if_failing: Limits are checked after provisioning or not at all.

scenarios.title: Cleanup deletes orphaned session namespaces but never foreign ones
scenarios.given: An orphan with session labels and namespaces that are unlabelled, partly labelled or belong to other teams
scenarios.when: The controller starts
scenarios.then: Only the fully labelled orphan is removed
scenarios.if_failing: Namespace deletion no longer verifies both ownership labels. This can delete other teams' workloads.

scenarios.title: An interrupted teardown completes after the outage
scenarios.when: The agent deletes its session and the controller later restarts with the cluster healthy
scenarios.then: First 202 with state tearing-down and deploys rejected with 409; after restart the namespace and record are gone
scenarios.if_failing: Teardown state is not persisted or the janitor does not retry.

scenarios.title: A failed apply leaves the session usable and hides internals
scenarios.given: A cluster that fails one create
scenarios.when: The agent deploys, then retries after recovery
scenarios.then: 502 without internal detail and nothing recorded; the retry succeeds
scenarios.if_failing: Deploy records partial state or leaks cluster error text to agents.

scenarios.title: Invalid agent configuration prevents startup
scenarios.given: An agents file with unknown fields, no policy, namespaces the policy forbids, an allowed RBAC kind, or empty content
scenarios.when: The controller starts
scenarios.then: It exits non-zero
scenarios.if_failing: Configuration is being accepted leniently. It must fail closed.

scenarios.title: Concurrent requests cannot exceed limits or overlap on one session
scenarios.when: They race
scenarios.then: Exactly max_sessions are created; deploys on one session never overlap; tearing-down sessions reject deploys; expired or foreign sessions are not found
scenarios.if_failing: A lock or ownership check in internal/session regressed.

scenarios.title: Real cluster: apply, label, diff and prune against kind
scenarios.given: kind, kubectl and a running Docker daemon
scenarios.when: .verify/e2e/kind.sh runs
scenarios.then: ConfigMaps are applied with ownership labels; diff-app reports unchanged; removing a manifest with prune deletes only that object
scenarios.if_failing: The fake API in .verify/integration may be hiding real API behaviour (defaults, field managers, discovery).
